blocks.text: Three Tiers of Polished Concrete Care

Polished concrete is popular in creative offices, tech campuses, and converted warehouse space because nightly maintenance is fast. In our pricing data, polished concrete carries a 0.95 flooring multiplier, meaning routine janitorial cleaning costs about 5% less than the carpet baseline. That savings is real, but it only holds if the floor's densified surface and guard coat stay intact. Concrete care breaks into three tiers: routine burnishing to restore sheen, periodic scrub and guard-coat sealing with optional densifier, and restoration grinding when the cream layer is worn, stained, or etched.

Each tier is priced differently. Burnishing is fast, often 4,000-8,000 sq ft per hour on open floors, so it is cheap per sq ft. Guard-coat sealing needs a deep scrub, dry time, and two thin coats, so productivity falls to 1,000-2,500 sq ft per hour. Re-grinding with metal or resin diamonds is a true construction-trade process measured in hundreds of square feet per hour.

blocks.text: Crack filling with semi-rigid polyurea runs about $4-$12 per lineal foot. Stain removal for oil, ink, or rust spots under desks and in breakrooms is usually billed hourly or as a $50-$150 per spot allowance, because results vary and some stains require spot grinding.
Worked Example: 12,000 sq ft Creative Office

A 12,000 sq ft open-plan office has 9,000 sq ft of polished concrete and 3,000 sq ft of carpet in conference rooms. Nightly janitorial at five nights a week falls in the 10,000-24,999 sq ft bracket at $0.07-$0.12 per sq ft per visit, about $18,190-$31,180 per month at 21.65 visits before flooring adjustments. The concrete program below sits on top of that base.

blocks.text: If the building moves from monthly to quarterly burnishing, the burnish line drops to $5,400 and the total to about $16,500, but gloss will fade faster in high-traffic lanes. Many offices split the difference: monthly burnishing in entries, corridors, and the kitchen; quarterly in low-traffic zones.

blocks.title: Benchmark: densifier is not an annual line item
blocks.text: Lithium or sodium silicate densifier chemically hardens the concrete surface and generally lasts years. Paying to re-densify every year is rarely necessary unless the floor was re-ground or the original densifier was skipped. Guard coats, by contrast, are sacrificial and do need periodic renewal.
Equipment That Keeps Burnish Costs Low

Small suites with polished concrete do not need a full-size burnisher. A 12-inch twin-brush unit such as the Koblenz P-4000 B, running at 1100 RPM on a 4.2 amp motor with a 50 ft cord, can maintain sheen around desks and in narrow corridors where large machines cannot fit. During the day, a quiet executive sweeper like the Rubbermaid Commercial 421588, with a 6.5-inch path and soft blades, picks up grit in conference rooms without disrupting meetings. For spot cleaning edges, baseboards, and spills, color-coded split microfiber such as the Rubbermaid HYGEN 16x16 cloths, rated for about 500 launderings, lifts residue without leaving lint on the sealed surface.

items: Use only diamond-impregnated or burnishing pads approved for polished concrete; red or green stripping pads scratch the surface.
Keep cleaner pH between 7 and 10; acidic products dissolve the cement paste and erode gloss.
Dry-dust mop before every burnish so grit does not get dragged under the pad.
Protect under-desk chair zones with clear chair mats to reduce rolling caster abrasion.
Wipe breakroom spills of coffee, citrus, or soda immediately to prevent etching.

blocks.title: Silica and chemical safety
blocks.text: Dry grinding concrete releases respirable crystalline silica regulated by OSHA. Require restoration vendors to use wet methods or HEPA vacuum dust extraction, and maintain SDS for densifiers and guard coats under HazCom. Routine burnishing does not trigger the silica standard, but grinding does.
How to Write a Concrete Care Scope

items.name: Classify the floor
items.text: Record the original polish level, grit, and whether a guard coat exists so vendors bid the right tier.

items.name: Separate routine from periodic
items.text: Keep nightly auto-scrubbing in the retainer and list burnishing and guard coats as scheduled periodic services.

items.name: Specify pads and chemistry
items.text: Name the pad grit system, neutral cleaner, and guard-coat product to prevent damaging substitutions.

items.name: Set a gloss target
items.text: Agree on gloss-meter readings or distinctness-of-image targets at fixed points for acceptance.

items.name: Price restoration separately
items.text: Request a per-sq-ft rate card for resin re-polish and re-grind so future repairs do not require a new bid.

faqs.q: Is polished concrete really cheaper to maintain than VCT?
faqs.a: For routine cleaning, yes. Our pricing model applies a 0.95 multiplier to polished concrete versus 1.04 for VCT, and polished concrete avoids the strip-and-recoat cycles VCT needs. The savings shrink if burnishing is skipped and the floor needs a resin re-polish at $2.50-$4.00 per sq ft.

faqs.q: Can the nightly janitorial crew handle burnishing?
faqs.a: Many can, using a high-speed burnisher or compact polisher with diamond-impregnated pads. Confirm the vendor's certificate of insurance covers floor-care damage and that the scope specifies pad type. Guard-coat application and any grinding are usually better assigned to a floor-care specialist.

faqs.q: How is monthly burnishing converted to a contract fee?
faqs.a: Multiply the burnished square footage by the unit price for one visit and by visits per month. Monthly equals one visit; biweekly equals about 2.17 visits based on 4.333 weeks per month. For 9,000 sq ft at $0.15 biweekly, that is roughly $2,930 per month.

faqs.q: Do green-certified offices restrict guard coats?
faqs.a: Buildings operating under LEED or Green Seal policies often require low-VOC, water-based guard coats and neutral cleaners. Ask vendors for product VOC data and SDS, and schedule application when ventilation can run overnight before occupants return.

faqs.q: What minimum charge should a small suite expect?
faqs.a: Minimums typically run $350-$750 per mobilization. A 1,500 sq ft suite at $0.20 per sq ft burnish would only be $300, so it will usually be billed the minimum. Bundling burnishing with carpet extraction or quarterly deep cleaning on the same night is the easiest way to get value out of that charge.
